Unknown error found?

messages.author: 55771919c42cb6a1
messages.subject: Re: numericInput widget arguments "min" and "max" do not show any effect
parts:
numericInput() emits HTML code like this:
<input id="in_numeric" type="number" value="5" min="1" max="10" step="0.5"/>

The browser then decides how to handle the input. At least in the latest version of Chrome, the numeric input lets you type in any number. However, if you click on the up and down arrows, it does restrict the values that are accessible.


If it's very important to validate the values, you should make sure to do it on the server side (although it's certainly not a bad thing to also validate on the client). Validating input on the client can of course make things easier for the user, but the user can hypothetically also modify the client-side code to send any values that they want.

-Winston

messages.subject: Re: numericInput widget arguments "min" and "max" do not show any effect
parts: That's entirely an HTML/IE problem and has nothing to do with Shiny really. If you really really wanted to use a javascript plugin to replace the numericinput (like the jquery thing suggested in the SO thread), you could technically do that, but it's not trivial and honestly not worth it.  The little arrows are not a very big feature, users can still input any number they want by typing it manually. I wouldn't worry about the arrows issue too much
